title: Netflix Has Used AI on About 300 Titles, but “Human Touch Is Critical,” Exec Says in Busan
key_facts: Sung Q Lee, Netflix's senior director of production for Asia-Pacific, said Netflix has used AI in various capacities on about 300 titles.
He spoke on Saturday (10 Oct 2026) at Netflix's Creative Asia event at the Busan International Film Festival, co-hosted with the Motion Picture Association.
Lee listed uses in previsualization, production design, set-dressing concepts, editing and VFX (visual effects).
He said “the human touch is critical and necessary” when it comes to conveying emotion.
Korean director Kang Yun-sung estimated AI cut about 40 percent from the financing needs of his new film “The Gulf of Aden”, which uses generative tools from China's Kling AI.
Kang's earlier AI-assisted feature “Run to the West” earned about $100,000 after bad buzz over its AI visuals.
Wētā FX's Kimball Thurston called the studio's use “assistive AI” that is not allowed to change creative intent.
The report says Hollywood is profoundly wary of AI while Asia's content sector mostly sees opportunity.
quote_evidence: Netflix has already used AI in various capacities on about 300 titles, one of its senior production executives said Saturday during an industry discussion at the Busan International Film Festival.
Kang estimated that the AI-assisted approach could reduce the film’s production costs by around 40 percent.

The occasion also highlighted just how differently the Hollywood creative community and Asian content sector tend to perceive the potential perils and promise of the technology, with the former profoundly wary and the latter seeing it mostly as an opportunity.
why_it_matters_hint: Netflix gives a number for its AI use while saying human creativity must stay central.
notes: Full text read. The 300-title figure is one executive's statement with no breakdown. Kang's 40 percent is his own estimate.
